title: Kedgeree
subtitle: Smoked haddock, rice, and egg breakfast
excerpt: The British-Indian breakfast dish: flaked smoked haddock folded through lightly spiced buttery rice with chopped hard-boiled eggs and fresh parsley. A dish that traces a line between Victorian Britain and the kitchens of the British Raj.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian dish derived from the Indian khichdi (a simple dish of rice and lentils spiced with cumin and mustard seeds). British soldiers and colonists adapted the dish during the Raj era, replacing the lentils with flaked fish (initially any cooked fish, later specifically smoked haddock) and adding hard-boiled eggs. The dish was adopted into Edwardian upper-class breakfast culture in Britain, where it was served alongside kippers and devilled kidneys on the sideboard as part of a lavish breakfast spread. It fell out of fashion in the mid-twentieth century but has returned to restaurant and home menus as part of a renewed interest in Anglo-Indian cooking. The spicing is gentle: curry powder, cumin, and bay leaves give warmth without heat.

content.text: Poach the smoked haddock in milk before flaking; the poaching liquid can be used to cook the rice, adding depth. Undercook the eggs slightly: they will be added hot to the hot rice and carry-cook a little further. Fold in the fish at the end and be gentle: you want large flakes, not fine shreds.

items.preparation: undyed if possible; poached in milk, skin and bones removed, flaked
for poaching the haddock; reserved for cooking the rice
hard-boiled for 8 minutes; peeled and quartered

content.text: Simmer the smoked haddock in the milk for 5 to 7 minutes until just cooked. Remove the fish, reserving the milk. Flake the fish into large pieces, discarding skin and bones. Cook the rice in the reserved milk topped up with water to the volume required; add the bay leaves during cooking. Drain and set aside.

Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the cumin seeds and curry powder and cook for 1 minute. Add the cooked rice and stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Fold in the flaked haddock and cream (if using) gently. Heat through for 2 minutes. Remove the bay leaves. Arrange the quartered eggs on top. Scatter with parsley. Serve with lemon wedges.
